q1: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2: SELECT PROJECT_ID , ROUND((SUM(EXPERIENCE_YEARS) / COUNT(P.EMPLOYEE_ID)),2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT P INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE E ON P.EMPLOYEE_ID = E.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY PROJECT_ID ORDER BY PROJECT_ID
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT PROJECT_ID , ROUND((SUM(EXPERIENCE_YEARS) / COUNT(P.EMPLOYEE_ID)),2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT P INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE E ON P.EMPLOYEE_ID = E.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY PROJECT_ID ORDER BY PROJECT_ID
explanation: Both queries aim to calculate the average years of experience for employees assigned to each project. They join the PROJECT and EMPLOYEE tables on EMPLOYEE_ID, group the results by PROJECT_ID, and use the AVG() function to compute the average experience years.
